sections.title: Habit and habitat
sections.text: Goat willow is a deciduous shrub or small tree of woodland edges, clearings and moist ground in Europe and Asia. It usually reaches 6–10 m, sometimes taller. Its broad oval leaves are green above and hairy, paler beneath.

sections.title: Spring catkins
sections.text: Catkins appear in early spring before the leaves. Male catkins are silky and silvery at first, turning yellow as the stamens open; female catkins are greener. The plate matches these catkins and the broad leaves.

sections.title: Uses and relation
sections.text: Goat willow provides early pollen and nectar for insects. Like other willows, its bark contains salicylates; medicinal preparations are not suitable for everyone. It differs from white willow (Salix alba) in its broader leaves and earlier catkins.
